title: Descent and associativity of witnessed comparison pastes
statement:
Use ordinary categories [def-nagata-category]. A functor preserves identities and composition; a natural transformation is a family of component maps commuting with every functorial arrow, and is a natural isomorphism when every component is invertible. Let $\mathscr B$ be a category. For each object $X$ give categories $\mathcal E_X,\mathcal P_X$ and a functor $N_X:\mathcal E_X\to\mathcal P_X$. For each arrow $f:X\to Y$ give a nonempty cofiltered category $I_f$ (any two objects admit a common source and parallel arrows can be equalized), and for $c\in I_f$ functors $F_f^{e,c}:\mathcal E_X\to\mathcal E_Y$, $F_f^{p,c}:\mathcal P_X\to\mathcal P_Y$, with natural isomorphisms $C_f^c:N_YF_f^{e,c}\cong F_f^{p,c}N_X$. Write composition functionally, with associators inserted. All pro-side refinement and tower transformations below are specified only on witnessed inputs: an input at $X$ is a pair $(E,\xi)$ with $E\in\mathcal E_X$ and an isomorphism $\xi:N_XE\cong M$ in $\mathcal P_X$. On such an input the value of a pro-side transformation is transported from its value at $N_XE$ by functorial application of $\xi$ and its inverse. Naturality of these transformations means naturality in $E$ and under these specified changes of witness, rather than naturality on all of $\mathcal P_X$. The isomorphism $C_f^c(E)$ gives $F_f^{p,c}N_XE$ the witness $F_f^{e,c}E$, so composites have such inputs as well.
For each refinement $u:c'\to c$ suppose given a coherent etale natural isomorphism $\rho_u^e:F_f^{e,c}\cong F_f^{e,c'}$ and a specified natural map $\rho_u^p:F_f^{p,c}\to F_f^{p,c'}$, satisfying
$$C_f^{c'}N_Y(\rho_u^e)=(\rho_u^pN_X)C_f^c.$$
Etale comparisons through common refinements are assumed independent of their arrows and satisfy the cocycle law. For each composable $f,g$ suppose supplied a nonempty collection of compatible tower choices of candidates for $f,g,gf$, any two admitting a common refining tower. Each chosen triple of candidates can be compared to a tower triple by refinement comparisons and their inverses. Suppose the etale tower maps $\alpha^e:F_g^eF_f^e\cong F_{gf}^e$ descend through these comparisons to choice-independent associative unital natural isomorphisms. Suppose the computed pro-side tower maps $\alpha^p:F_g^pF_f^p\to F_{gf}^p$ are natural and obey on each tower
$$C_{gf}N_Z(\alpha^e)=(\alpha^pN_X)(F_g^pC_f)(C_gF_f^e).$$
Assume also that $C_{\mathrm{id}}$ is the identity under the specified identity-functor identifications. For arbitrary candidates define the pro-side composition by moving to a tower, using its computed map, and moving back, with the specified pro-side refinement maps evaluated on $N_X(-)$; at other witnessed inputs use conjugation by the displayed $C$ witnesses.
Then every $\rho_u^pN_X$ is invertible and equals $C_f^{c'}N_Y(\rho_u^e)(C_f^c)^{-1}$. All common-refinement comparisons on the image of $N_X$ are independent of choices and satisfy identities, composition and the cocycle law. The computed tower maps descend to arbitrary candidates, independently of the common refining tower, and satisfy the same displayed composition equation there. They equal transport through $C$, are invertible on witnessed inputs, and are unital and associative there. More explicitly, for composable $f,g,h$ both pro-side triple maps after precomposition by
$$D=(F_h^pF_g^pC_f)\circ(F_h^pC_gF_f^e)\circ(C_hF_g^eF_f^e)$$
equal $C_{hgf}N(\alpha^e_{\rm triple})$. These assertions are natural in the input. Only evaluations at objects with their specified $C$ witnesses are asserted; no fullness, faithfulness or essential surjectivity of the $N_X$ is required.

proof.text: Work componentwise, in the functional composition convention of the statement. All reassociations are the canonical functor associators, whose components are identities. Suppress object arguments when they are determined. Write $E_f=F_f^{e,c}$, $P_f=F_f^{p,c}$ and $C_f:N_YE_f\cong P_fN_X$. The category laws of [def-nagata-category] allow cancellation of an isomorphism: from $a s=b s$ compose on the right with $s^{-1}$. Functors preserve inverses since $F(s)F(s^{-1})=F(ss^{-1})=1$ and conversely. These component identities justify every cancellation and inversion below; they do not require any property of $N_X$ beyond functoriality.

source.place: Tag 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined), cancellation footnote; componentwise categorical calculation

proof.text:
For $u:c'\to c$, the assumed refinement square gives, by right-composition with $C_c^{-1}$,
$$\rho_u^pN_X=C_{c'}N_Y(\rho_u^e)C_c^{-1}.$$
Its inverse is $C_cN_Y((\rho_u^e)^{-1})C_{c'}^{-1}$, as multiplying in either order gives the identity. More generally any finite refinement zigzag from $c$ to $d$, with etale composite $t:E_c\to E_d$, has pro-side composite $C_dN_Y(t)C_c^{-1}$: substitute the displayed formula (or its inverse) at each edge and cancel each adjacent $C^{-1}C$. This also proves the assertion for a single identity or two composable refinement arrows.

For candidates $c,d$ and a common source $r$, write $a:E_c\to E_r$ and $b:E_d\to E_r$ for the etale refinement maps. The resulting comparison $c\to d$ on the pro side is
$$ (C_rN(b)C_d^{-1})^{-1}(C_rN(a)C_c^{-1})=C_dN(b^{-1}a)C_c^{-1}.$$
The hypothesis on etale common-refinement comparisons makes $t_{dc}=b^{-1}a$ independent of the common source and its arrows. Thus this pro comparison is independent too. For three candidates, its cocycle law is the explicit cancellation
$$C_eN(t_{ed})C_d^{-1}C_dN(t_{dc})C_c^{-1}=C_eN(t_{ed}t_{dc})C_c^{-1}=C_eN(t_{ec})C_c^{-1}.$$
The identity comparison is $C_cN(1)C_c^{-1}=1$. Common sources exist by the stated cofilteredness; no colimit or smallness theorem is used.

source.place: Tag 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined), common refinements and choice independence

proof.text:
Fix a composable pair and a candidate triple, and put
$$B_{g,f}=(P_g C_f)(C_g E_f):N_ZE_gE_f\cong P_gP_fN_X.$$
On a compatible tower the assumed equation uniquely determines the computed map by
$$A_{g,f}N_X=C_{gf}N_Z(\alpha^e_{g,f})B_{g,f}^{-1}.$$
An explicit inverse is $B_{g,f}N_Z((\alpha^e_{g,f})^{-1})C_{gf}^{-1}$. Each factor is invertible by hypothesis and Step 1. In particular this establishes invertibility only at image inputs; it asserts nothing at an unwitnessed object of $\mathcal P_X$.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), tower composition; assumed tower equation solved for its map

proof.text:
Check the input comparison when candidates for $f,g$ change. Let $t_f:E_f\to E_f'$ and $t_g:E_g\to E_g'$ be etale comparisons, and let $s_f,s_g$ be their pro comparisons from Step 3. Set
$$t=(E_g't_f)(t_gE_f),\qquad S=(P_g's_f)(s_gP_f).$$
At the second occurrence, $s_g$ is evaluated using the displayed $C_f$ witness. Its stipulated naturality under this change of witness says
$$s_g(P_fN_X)(P_gC_f)=(P_g'C_f)s_g(N_YE_f).$$
Substitute this into $SB_{g,f}$, then use the two refinement equations from Step 2 and naturality of $C_g'$ at $t_f$. The factors become, in order,
$$(P_g'C_f')(P_g'N_Y(t_f))(C_g'E_f)N_Z(t_gE_f)
=(P_g'C_f')(C_g'E_f')N_Z((E_g't_f)(t_gE_f))=B'_{g,f}N_Z(t).$$
For a change of the $gf$ candidate with etale comparison $q:E_{gf}\to E_{gf}'$, its pro comparison $Q$ satisfies $QC_{gf}=C_{gf}'N_Z(q)$ directly by Step 3. These equations also hold for inverse comparisons by multiplication by their inverses.

source.place: Tags 0F7I and 0F7J (lemma-shriek-well-defined, lemma-shriek-composition), compatibility of input and output comparisons

proof.text:
For arbitrary fixed candidates choose a tower triple. Let $t$ compare their etale input composite to the tower input composite, and $q$ compare the tower output candidate back to their output candidate. The pro input and output comparisons $S,Q$ of Step 5 satisfy $SB=B_{\rm tower}N(t)$ and $QC_{\rm tower}=C_{gf}N(q)$. Hence their computed paste $A=QA_{\rm tower}S$ satisfies
$$AB=QC_{\rm tower}N(\alpha^e_{\rm tower})N(t)=C_{gf}N(q\alpha^e_{\rm tower}t)=C_{gf}N(\alpha^e_{g,f}).$$
The last equality is precisely the assumed etale descent through candidate comparisons. Thus $A=C_{gf}N(\alpha^e_{g,f})B^{-1}$, independently of the chosen tower and of the comparison paths. This proves agreement on common refining towers as well. It gives both the required equation and invertibility for arbitrary candidates without assuming any unproved pro-side descent.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), independence of chosen compatible tower; cancellation calculation

proof.text:
For a triple $f,g,h$, put $D=(P_hP_gC_f)(P_hC_gE_f)(C_hE_gE_f)$ as in the statement. For the parenthesization $L=A_{h,gf}(P_hA_{g,f})$, substitute Step 6 first for $A_{g,f}$ and then for $A_{h,gf}$. Cancelling the adjacent inverse comparisons gives
$$LD=C_{hgf}N(\alpha^e_{h,gf})(C_hE_{gf})^{-1}(P_hN(\alpha^e_{g,f}))(C_hE_gE_f).$$
Naturality of $C_h$ at $\alpha^e_{g,f}$ identifies the last three factors with $N(E_h\alpha^e_{g,f})$. Therefore
$$LD=C_{hgf}N(\alpha^e_{h,gf}(E_h\alpha^e_{g,f})).$$
Every cancellation here takes place in the output category; $N$ is never cancelled or used to reflect an equality.

source.place: Tag 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor), first triple-composition path; explicit comparison calculation

proof.text:
For the other parenthesization $R=A_{hg,f}(A_{h,g}P_f)$, naturality at the specified witness $C_f$ gives
$$(A_{h,g}P_fN_X)(P_hP_gC_f)=(P_{hg}C_f)(A_{h,g}N_YE_f).$$
Consequently Step 6 applied at $E_f$ gives
$$RD=A_{hg,f}(P_{hg}C_f)(C_{hg}E_f)N(\alpha^e_{h,g}E_f)
=C_{hgf}N(\alpha^e_{hg,f}(\alpha^e_{h,g}E_f)).$$
The two etale composites in Steps 7 and 8 are the same $\alpha^e_{\rm triple}$ by the assumed etale associativity. Thus both pro composites precomposed by $D$ equal $C_{hgf}N(\alpha^e_{\rm triple})$. Since $D$ is invertible they agree. This uses only binary compatible towers, already handled in Step 6; no existence of an additional triple tower is needed.

source.place: Tag 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor), second triple-composition path and equality

proof.text: For a pair containing an identity arrow, the given identity-functor identifications and $C_{\mathrm{id}}=1$ give $B=C_f$. The assumed etale unit law gives $\alpha^e=1$ under those identifications. Step 6 therefore gives $A=C_fN(1)C_f^{-1}=1$, proving both unit laws. All formulas above are natural in $E$: move a morphism $E\to E'$ past each factor using the given naturality squares; an inverse square follows by multiplying the original square by the two component inverses, and pasted squares follow by substitution and cancellation.

source.place: Tags 0F7I and 0F7K (lemma-shriek-well-defined, lemma-pseudo-functor), identities and naturality

proof.text:
Finally let $(E,\xi:N_XE\cong M)$ be a witnessed input. For any transformation $T:U\to V$ occurring above its value there is, by the stated witness convention,
$$T_{(E,\xi)}=V(\xi)T_{N_XE}U(\xi)^{-1}.$$
If $T$ is invertible on the image its inverse at this input is $U(\xi)T_{N_XE}^{-1}V(\xi)^{-1}$. For a composite $T_2T_1$ the middle functorial images of $\xi^{-1}\xi$ cancel, so every equation proved on image inputs remains the same equation at witnessed inputs. The intervening witness for $P_fM$ is $P_f(\xi)C_f(E):N_YE_fE\cong P_fM$; this is exactly the witness used in Steps 5 and 8. This proves naturality under the stipulated changes of witness and all asserted witnessed identities. It makes no assertion comparing unrelated witnesses through an arrow not supplied by the hypotheses, and proves no naturality on all of $\mathcal P_X$.
